answer: DeepWalk is reported to remain strong on the Flickr and BlogCatalog multi-label classification tasks even when labeled training data is sparse. In the original evaluation, the method was tested under reduced training-data settings, including using 60% less labeled training data than the full setting. Under this sparse-label regime, DeepWalk still produced competitive classification performance, indicating that the learned node embeddings preserve useful local and global network structure for downstream multi-label classification. The key takeaway is that performance degrades gracefully rather than collapsing when labeled supervision is substantially reduced, which is one of the main motivations for using random-walk-based network embedding methods in low-label regimes. I cannot give exact numeric scores from memory with high confidence, but the qualitative result is that DeepWalk remains effective on both Flickr and BlogCatalog under substantial label sparsity.
